text:
experiment: permutation-brier-v1
question: does permutation averaging improve Jev's forecast of the sealed outcome?
outcome: rule native-retention-6h-v1 (ops/journal/resolution-rule.json), unchanged
arms, one journal action each, never pooled:
  wallet_promotion@heuristic  confidence = transfer-size heuristic (confidenceFromValue)
  wallet_promotion@single     confidence = Jev P(retains), options in canonical order [retains, declines]
  wallet_promotion@permuted   confidence = mean Jev P(retains) over both orderings
pairing: single and permuted come from the SAME Jev request -- single is ordering 0 of the permuted call
egress: value_pls, balance_pls, fraction_sent only; the address is not sent
forecast scale: P(retains) in both Jev arms -- same scale, so Brier is comparable
metric: Brier(single) - Brier(permuted), over wallets resolved in BOTH arms
minimum: 97 paired resolved wallets; below that the verdict is UNDERPOWERED, not a result
prediction: Brier(single) - Brier(permuted) >= 0.02
pre-data measurement 2026-09-23 (3 wallets x 5 identical calls):
  permuted P(retains) ~= 2x single (0.30/0.16, 0.22/0.10, 0.35/0.17): the 2nd-listed option is favoured
  P2 falsified: averaging did not reduce call-to-call spread (1/3 wallets)
  P3 held: cross-wallet mean range 0.064 -- these features barely discriminate
